 Darius Garland, Kris Dunn, Derrick Jones Jr., Rui Hachimura and Isaiah Jackson will start Wednesday’s game against the Kings. 
 Dunn is good to go after missing most of the preseason with a minor injury, and he’ll start alongside Garland in the backcourt. Clippers head coach Tyronn Lue said on Saturday that Jackson would start at center, so his inclusion is unsurprising. Garland and Hachimura should lead the starters offensively. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson 
 Source:  Tomer Azarly

 Isaiah Jackson accounted for 13 points (6-of-8 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), five rebounds and one steal in Wednesday’s win over the Kings. 
 Jackson’s starting nod was expected to raise his fantasy ceiling, and he was productive Wednesday night. However, the Clippers’ center played just 15 minutes because of foul trouble. Backup Brook Lopez played 27 minutes, and that may not have happened if Jackson were able to stay on the court. Jackson is worth a look in 12-team leagues if he’s on the waiver wire, even with the foul trouble against Sacramento. 
 Isaiah Jackson 
 LAC 
 Forward 
 #23 
 Clippers head coach Tyronn Lue said Saturday that Isaiah Jackson will begin the regular season as the team’s starting center. 
 Jackson was the starter throughout the preseason, so Saturday’s news is not a complete surprise. However, the confirmation makes him an even better option for fantasy managers who need a center in the later rounds of their drafts. Brook Lopez will be the backup, and that limits his fantasy value considerably. 
 Isaiah Jackson 
 LAC 
 Forward 
 #23 
 Isaiah Jackson accounted for nine points (4-of-8 FGs), five rebounds, three assists, one steal and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s exhibition against the Nuggets. 
 Wednesday’s game was the Clippers’ last preseason game, so it’s fair to question how much of a “dress rehearsal” it was for Tyronn Lue’s team. Jackson started again and played 26 minutes, while veteran Brook Lopez (nine points, two rebounds, one assist and one three-pointer) logged eight minutes off the bench. If Jackson can lock down the starting job, his upside would make him worthy of late-round consideration in drafts. And even if he doesn’t start, the Clippers will be light on centers until Yanic Konan Niederhäuser is cleared to return from the foot injury that ended his 2025-26 season in March. 
 Jordan Miller 
 LAC 
 Guard 
 #22 
 ESPN’s Shams Charania reports that Jordan Miller underwent surgery on a torn left rotator cuff and will be reevaluated in six months. 
 Miller’s injury could mean additional run for Keaton Wagler and Kris Dunn, though the pair will compete with Gradey Dick, Bradley Beal and Darius Garland for minutes. 
 Max Strus 
 LAC 
 Guard-Forward 
 #2 
 Max Strus has been traded to the Clippers as part of the three-team deal that sent Peyton Watson to the Cavaliers. 
 Strus will get a fresh start after three seasons in Cleveland. His defense and floor spacing should help make an immediate impact for the Clippers as they look to establish a new identity in the post-Kawhi Leonard era. Strus could start alongside Darius Garland, but his presence in a crowded backcourt will make the rotation difficult to project. Kris Dunn, Bennedict Mathurin (RFA) and Gradey Dick all stand to lose out on minutes with Strus on the squad. 
 Isaiah Jackson 
 LAC 
 Forward 
 #23 
 Isaiah Jackson (ankle) is available to play against the Warriors on Wednesday. 
 Jackson will be good to go, making this his first appearance since March 27. He has typically filled out the backup center minutes behind Brook Lopez, but in an elimination game, the rotations could look different, especially since it has been nearly three weeks since Jackson last suited up. 
 Isaiah Jackson 
 LAC 
 Forward 
 #23 
 Isaiah Jackson (ankle) has been upgraded to probable for Wednesday’s game against the Warriors. 
 Jackson has been sidelined since March 27, but after practicing fully on Tuesday, he is now expected to make his return for the Clippers’ win-or-go-home matchup with the Warriors. He’ll likely occupy some of the backup center minutes behind Brook Lopez. 
 Isaiah Jackson 
 LAC 
 Forward 
 #23 
 Isaiah Jackson (ankle) fully participated in Tuesday’s practice, including 5-on-5. 
 Jackson has been out since spraining his ankle during a March 27 win over the Pacers, leaving the Clippers without a legitimate backup center. John Collins has filled the void in Jackson’s absence and would continue to do so if he can’t return for Wednesday’s Play-In Tournament game against the Warriors. 
 John Collins 
 LAC 
 Forward-Center 
 #20 
 John Collins accounted for 18 points (8-of-12 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs) and nine rebounds in Sunday’s win over the Warriors. 
 With no Kawhi Leonard (ankle), Collins returned to the Clippers’ starting lineup after coming off the bench in three of the previous four games. He finished one rebound shy of a double-double against the Warriors, but Collins produced nothing else in his 21 minutes on the floor. Leonard will be available for Wednesday’s rematch with the Warriors, which would relegate Collins to the backup center role he’s been asked to assume since Isaiah Jackson went down. 
 Isaiah Jackson 
 LAC 
 Forward 
 #23 
 Isaiah Jackson (ankle) is out for Sunday’s game against the Warriors. 
 Jackson has been out since March 27, and he will remain out for Sunday’s season finale. John Collins has served as the backup center, a role that eventually prompted Clippers head coach Tyronn Lue to move him to the bench. With Kawhi Leonard (ankle) questionable, Collins’ opportunities may increase on Sunday.

 Naz Reid had 17 points (7-of-16 FGs), six rebounds, two assists, one steal and three three-pointers against the Hawks on Friday. 
 Reid had seven turnovers despite only playing 24 minutes and that’s a crusher in nine-category leagues. Otherwise, he’s scored 37 points on 15-of-34 attempts with seven three-pointers in his first two games with the Hornets. That’ll play. If Reid can keep the turnovers under control, he’s well on his way to paying off his mid-round draft price.

 Miles McBride produced 20 points (6-of-9 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), two rebounds, one assist, one steal and six three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Celtics.
 McBride rebounded nicely from his poor showing in Tuesday’s loss to the 76ers, a game in which he scored three points on 1-of-5 shooting. Against the Celtics, Deuce shot 6-of-8 from three and scored 20 of the Knicks’ 32 bench points. The reserve role doesn’t help McBride deliver consistent fantasy value, but he can be an effective source of points and three-pointers in deep leagues.

 Jalen Brunson accumulated 19 points (7-of-17 FGs, 3-of-6 FTs), two rebounds, four assists, two blocks and two three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Celtics.
 Brunson’s gotten off to a slow start by his standards, shooting 13-of-32 from the field in New York’s first two games. The Knicks star also didn’t shoot well from the foul line, missing three of his six attempts in Boston. Those rostering Brunson don’t have much to worry about, as the season is only two games old. However, they would certainly like to see him clean up his shooting in Sunday’s game against the Magic.

 Jalen Johnson had 19 points (9-of-16 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), seven rebounds, eight assists, three steals and one block in Friday’s game against the Hornets. 
 With less than two minutes left in the first half, Dyson Daniel hit the floor for one of his seven steals, leading to a Jalen Johnson alley-oop dunk on the other end. That pretty much encapsulates how the night went for the Hawks as Johnson led the team in scoring with 19 in the 128-81 blowout win. Johnson showed he was able to move past the extracurriculars with the Magic on Wednesday with his usual excellent performance against the Hornets. 
 -  Nick Shlain

 OG Anunoby finished Friday’s loss to the Celtics with 20 points (5-of-11 FGs, 8-of-10 FTs), 10 rebounds, eight assists and two three-pointers.
 After scoring 10 points on 3-of-12 shooting in Tuesday’s loss to the 76ers, Anunoby was much better offensively on Friday. An 8-of-10 night at the foul line boosted his point total, and the Knicks forward shot just under 50 percent from the field. Add in the rebounds and assists, and this was a solid night for those rostering Anunoby.

 Karl-Anthony Towns accounted for 22 points (9-of-13 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), 10 rebounds, three assists, one steal and two three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Celtics.
 After struggling with early foul trouble in Tuesday’s loss to the 76ers, Towns did not commit a foul during the first quarter of Friday’s game. The bad news is that he made up for it by committing three fouls in the second quarter. Towns finished with a solid overall line, and avoiding early foul trouble let him log 37 minutes. He’ll look to build on Friday’s productive effort when the Knicks host the Magic on Sunday.

 Neemias Queta tallied 15 points (4-of-8 FGs, 6-of-9 FTs), six rebounds, one assist, three blocks and one three-pointer in Friday’s win over the Knicks.
 The Celtics’ minutes split at center is worth tracking early in this season. Queta once again came off the bench on Friday, playing as many minutes (22) as starter Mitchell Robinson (four points, four rebounds, two assists and one blocked shot). Queta still had a good night, showing why fantasy managers should not give up on him. While he may not play starters’ minutes, Queta can still offer value in a reserve role.

 Dyson Daniels had 11 points (5-of-10 FGs, 1-of-3 FTs), nine rebounds, four assists, seven steals and one block in the Hawks’ 128-81 victory over the Hornets on Friday. 
 Daniels has now recorded at least five steals in consecutive games to start the season. The 23-year-old point guard leads the NBA in steals since the beginning of the 2024-25 season. The question is no longer whether he’ll lead the league in steals again this year, but by how many.
